method.purpose: Turn a technical SEO audit into replayable controls, observable evidence and an explicit decision.
method.scope: Thirteen domains and forty-four controls. The number of controls varies with risk; the grid predicts neither rankings nor traffic.
method.decision_rule: NO-GO when at least one Blocking control is Non-compliant, or when an applicable Blocking control remains Not tested. Decision required when a Major non-compliance remains. GO with reservations in all other cases, under the responsibility of the decision owner.

controls.control: The final page returns an actionable HTTP status code.
controls.method: Send a GET request, follow redirects and record the final status code.
controls.expected_evidence: Tested URL, timestamp and final 200 status for a public canonical page.
controls.limitation: A test from one IP does not prove the response received by Googlebot.

controls.control: Redirects are intentional, direct and loop-free.
controls.method: Test HTTP/HTTPS, host, trailing-slash and legacy URL variants, including the redirect count.
controls.expected_evidence: One final destination, documented chain and no loop.
controls.limitation: A valid redirect does not prove the semantic relevance of its destination.

controls.control: Server errors and soft 404s do not replace an explicit response.
controls.method: Test an existing page, a removed URL and a non-existent URL; compare status and content.
controls.expected_evidence: Consistent 4xx/5xx responses and an error template that does not return 200 by default.
controls.limitation: The final soft-404 classification remains a search-engine decision.

controls.control: robots.txt is accessible, parseable and does not block required resources.
controls.method: Fetch /robots.txt and inspect its content type, groups and applicable rules.
controls.expected_evidence: A 200 response, readable syntax and rules tied to a documented intent.
controls.limitation: robots.txt is a crawling protocol, not an access-control mechanism.

controls.control: A Disallow rule is never presented as a guarantee of deindexing.
controls.method: Compare the robots policy, indexing requirements and meta/X-Robots-Tag directives.
controls.expected_evidence: Separate decisions for crawling, indexing and protection.
controls.limitation: A blocked URL may remain known and appear without a snippet.

controls.control: Sensitive areas genuinely deny access at server level.
controls.method: Test private routes without a session and verify authentication, authorisation and caching.
controls.expected_evidence: A 401/403 response or authentication redirect, with no sensitive content delivered.
controls.limitation: Absence from the index is not proof of confidentiality.

controls.control: Robots meta directives and X-Robots-Tag match the page objective.
controls.method: Inspect headers and source DOM across indexable and excluded templates.
controls.expected_evidence: One directive or a compatible combination, with no accidental noindex.
controls.limitation: The engine must be allowed to crawl the resource to read the directive.

controls.control: The actual indexing status is checked in Search Console.
controls.method: Use URL Inspection on a representative sample and retain the export or screenshot.
controls.expected_evidence: Known URL, crawling permission, indexing state and Google-selected canonical documented.
controls.limitation: A public audit cannot establish this status without property access.

controls.control: Intentional exclusions have an owner and a rationale.
controls.method: Tie each excluded family to a rule, owner and review date.
controls.expected_evidence: Exclusion register: page type, mechanism, rationale, owner and review.
controls.limitation: The business relevance of an exclusion cannot be automated.

controls.control: Each canonical page publishes an absolute, stable and consistent URL.
controls.method: Compare the final URL, rel=canonical, sitemap and internal links.
controls.expected_evidence: Signals converge on the same canonical URL without a chain.
controls.limitation: rel=canonical is a strong signal, not a guaranteed directive.

controls.control: Genuine duplicate variants converge without hiding distinct pages.
controls.method: Sample parameters, pagination, filters and print versions; compare content and canonicals.
controls.expected_evidence: Documented mapping between each duplicate and its relevant canonical.
controls.limitation: Computed similarity does not replace an editorial decision.

controls.control: Google’s selected canonical is compared with the declared canonical.
controls.method: Inspect priority URLs and record the user-declared and Google-selected canonicals.
controls.expected_evidence: Agreement or a qualified, addressed divergence.
controls.limitation: Google’s selected canonical can change after recrawling.

controls.control: The sitemap contains only useful absolute canonical URLs.
controls.method: Parse every sitemap, count URLs and compare status, canonical and indexability.
controls.expected_evidence: Inventory without redirects, 4xx responses, noindex pages or duplicate canonicals.
controls.limitation: Sitemap inclusion does not guarantee indexing.

controls.control: lastmod reflects a significant change to the page.
controls.method: Compare lastmod with editorial history or a significant content deployment.
controls.expected_evidence: ISO 8601 timestamp tied to an actual change, not file generation.
controls.limitation: The engine may ignore a lastmod it considers unreliable.

controls.control: Sitemap size and segmentation limits are respected.
controls.method: Check uncompressed size, URL count, sitemap indexes and encoding.
controls.expected_evidence: No more than 50,000 URLs and 50 MB uncompressed per sitemap.
controls.limitation: A valid file can still cover the wrong editorial scope.

controls.control: Every important page receives at least one crawlable internal link.
controls.method: Crawl from public entry points and list pages with no incoming HTML link.
controls.expected_evidence: Link source, destination, anchor and destination status.
controls.limitation: The presence of a link does not prove its editorial value.

controls.control: Essential links use an a element with a resolvable href.
controls.method: Compare source and rendered DOM; identify buttons, onclick handlers and anchors without href.
controls.expected_evidence: A crawlable HTML link to every essential destination.
controls.limitation: Crawlability guarantees neither indexing nor rankings.

controls.control: Depth and orphan pages are measured within an explicit scope.
controls.method: Compare crawl, sitemap and CMS export; qualify every difference.
controls.expected_evidence: Orphan list, observed minimum depth and a decision for each family.
controls.limitation: No universal depth guarantees rankings.

controls.control: Parameters, filters and calendars do not create an infinite URL space.
controls.method: Group URLs by pattern, count combinations and look for crawl traps.
controls.expected_evidence: Indexing and navigation rule for each parameter pattern.
controls.limitation: The actual crawled volume requires logs or Search Console.

controls.control: The URL structure is readable, stable and correctly encoded.
controls.method: Identify spaces, fragments, encoded characters, case and volatile identifiers.
controls.expected_evidence: Documented URL patterns and no unintended variants.
controls.limitation: A readable URL is not sufficient evidence of SEO performance.

controls.control: Discovered but unindexed URLs are investigated by family.
controls.method: Segment the Pages report by template and compare it with sitemaps and logs.
controls.expected_evidence: Hypothesis per family, URL sample and post-fix result.
controls.limitation: A Search Console label describes a state, not always its cause.

controls.control: Each hreflang variant points to an indexable canonical URL.
controls.method: Parse HTML, HTTP or sitemap annotations and resolve every URL.
controls.expected_evidence: Valid language/region, 200 response and consistent canonical.
controls.limitation: hreflang helps targeting; it does not replace genuinely localised content.

controls.control: hreflang annotations are reciprocal and include the current page.
controls.method: Build variant clusters and verify return links and self-references.
controls.expected_evidence: Complete reciprocal cluster with no conflicting URL.
controls.limitation: A valid cluster does not prove the engine will always serve the expected variant.

controls.control: x-default represents a neutral destination or an explicit default variant.
controls.method: Check its presence and role in every relevant multilingual cluster.
controls.expected_evidence: Documented, accessible x-default URL consistent with the journey.
controls.limitation: x-default is not mandatory in every case.

controls.control: Critical content exists in source HTML or becomes observable after rendering.
controls.method: Compare the HTML response, rendered DOM and URL Inspection for critical elements.
controls.expected_evidence: Title, content, links, canonical and structured data present at the right stage.
controls.limitation: A local browser does not reproduce Google’s rendering exactly.

controls.control: Resources required for rendering are neither blocked nor failing.
controls.method: Inspect network activity, robots rules, CSP and console errors on priority templates.
controls.expected_evidence: Critical resources accessible and no error removes essential content.
controls.limitation: An error-free console does not prove indexing.

controls.control: SPA states and routes produce shareable URLs and consistent server responses.
controls.method: Open routes directly and test refresh, history, canonical and HTTP status.
controls.expected_evidence: Each indexable view has its own URL, 200 response, content and signals.
controls.limitation: Choosing SSR, CSR or SSG is not in itself an SEO guarantee.

controls.control: The document exposes an understandable HTML structure independently of appearance.
controls.method: Inspect title, language, main landmark, heading levels, links and labels on a sample.
controls.expected_evidence: Logical structure, one identifiable main subject and accessible components.
controls.limitation: Syntax validity alone proves neither quality nor relevance.

controls.control: Essential content remains available when scripts or styles fail.
controls.method: Test source HTML, disabled JavaScript and degraded network conditions.
controls.expected_evidence: Primary information and navigation remain available, or a fallback is documented.
controls.limitation: Acceptable degradation depends on the component’s function.

controls.control: Essential metadata is unique, visible and consistent with the page.
controls.method: Compare title, description, H1, Open Graph and main content by template.
controls.expected_evidence: Consistent topic and promise without mechanical duplication.
controls.limitation: Google may rewrite the title link or snippet in search results.

controls.control: JSON-LD describes entities that are visible and appropriate to the content.
controls.method: Compare each important property with visible content and type-specific guidance.
controls.expected_evidence: Valid, consistent graph with no invented entity or rating.
controls.limitation: Valid markup guarantees neither a rich result nor higher rankings.

controls.control: Stable @id values connect the same entities without creating duplicates.
controls.method: Build the graph and identify unnamed nodes, variable identifiers and duplicates.
controls.expected_evidence: Organization, Person, WebSite, WebPage and Article connected by stable @id values.
controls.limitation: Schema.org defines a vocabulary; interpretation depends on the consumer.

controls.control: Errors, warnings and unsupported uses are distinguished.
controls.method: Test Schema.org syntax and Google eligibility separately; record both results.
controls.expected_evidence: Report with no blocking error and qualified warnings.
controls.limitation: Rich Results Test does not validate the whole Schema.org vocabulary.

controls.control: Field Core Web Vitals are read at the 75th percentile.
controls.method: Record LCP, INP and CLS from field data by device type and URL group.
controls.expected_evidence: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms and CLS ≤ 0.1 at the 75th percentile for a Good assessment.
controls.limitation: Missing CrUX data does not mean the page is fast.

controls.control: Laboratory tests support diagnosis rather than simulate field data.
controls.method: Retain URL, device, network profile, tool version and detailed metrics.
controls.expected_evidence: Reproducible Lighthouse/WebPageTest report tied to a remediation hypothesis.
controls.limitation: A Lighthouse score of 100 guarantees neither field CWV nor rankings.

controls.control: Monitoring connects Search Console, logs and deployments to decision dates.
controls.method: Create a pre-change baseline, then verify at D+1, D+7 and D+30 according to risk.
controls.expected_evidence: Deployment log, crawl/indexing anomalies and signed decisions.
controls.limitation: Temporal correlation is not sufficient to attribute a traffic change.

controls.control: HTTPS, HSTS and embedded resources create neither certificate errors nor mixed content.
controls.method: Test certificates on public hosts, follow HTTP/HTTPS variants, record Strict-Transport-Security and find HTTP subresources.
controls.expected_evidence: Valid certificate for each host, HTTPS redirect, documented HSTS header and no active HTTP resource.
controls.limitation: HSTS strengthens transport after the policy is received; it fixes neither an invalid certificate nor a poor URL architecture.

controls.control: Host, case and trailing-slash variants converge on one rule.
controls.method: Replay www/non-www, HTTP/HTTPS, relevant case and trailing-slash variants on sample routes; compare redirect, canonical, sitemap and links.
controls.expected_evidence: One stable final URL per resource, no chain and consistent internal signals.
controls.limitation: Case can be significant depending on the server and application; the rule must be tested, not assumed.

controls.control: The CDN, Vary and geolocation do not serve contradictory SEO signals.
controls.method: Compare status, canonical, robots, language and content across regions or cache keys; inspect Vary, geolocation redirects and edge rules.
controls.expected_evidence: Identical SEO signals for the same URL, or explicitly documented variants accessible to Googlebot.
controls.source_scope: RFC 9110 defines Vary and HTTP response semantics. Google separately documents locale-adaptive page behaviour.
controls.limitation: Two test locations do not cover every route, POP or cache key.

controls.control: The chosen hreflang method — HTML, HTTP header or sitemap — is complete and unique.
controls.method: Identify the source of truth, then verify that every URL lists itself and all alternatives in that method.
controls.expected_evidence: Equivalent reciprocal clusters; when sitemaps are used, valid xhtml namespace and entries per URL.
controls.limitation: Combining HTML, headers and sitemaps offers no search benefit and increases divergence risk.

controls.control: Critical SEO invariants are replayed automatically before and after deployment.
controls.method: Run a representative URL set in CI: final status, redirects, robots/noindex, canonical, hreflang, server content, essential links and JSON-LD.
controls.expected_evidence: Versioned command, timestamped output, explicit failure threshold and link to the relevant deployment.
controls.source_label: Edikka method · no single primary source
controls.source_scope: Edikka governance and non-regression control; no single official document prescribes this complete pipeline.
controls.limitation: CI validates known invariants; it replaces neither Search Console, logs nor editorial review.

controls.control: Each AI crawler is governed according to its actual purpose: search, user action or training.
controls.method: Map search, user action and training separately — for example OAI-SearchBot / ChatGPT-User / GPTBot and Claude-SearchBot / Claude-User / ClaudeBot — to a dated decision and owner.
controls.expected_evidence: Table of user agent, purpose, rule, operator source and review date, without conflating live search with training.
controls.limitation: A robots directive is declarative; it proves neither the requester’s identity nor compliance by every operator.

controls.control: Access for authorised crawlers is tested with the full user-agent string and reconciled with logs.
controls.method: Send a GET request using the documented full user-agent, record status and redirects, find the request in logs and verify identity when the operator publishes a method.
controls.expected_evidence: Command, full string, final response, timestamp, server trace and verified/unverified identity status.
controls.limitation: Imitating a user agent does not reproduce crawler infrastructure; the test validates application policy, not a real operator visit.

controls.control: Critical content and evidence remain accessible without undocumented JavaScript execution.
controls.method: Compare raw HTML, rendered content and any public machine-readable resource; verify titles, facts, sources, links and update date.
controls.expected_evidence: Essential facts and sources in server HTML or a linked public resource, with a consistent version and stable URL.
controls.source_scope: Partial scope: Google documents JavaScript rendering for Google Search. This control cautiously extends verification to consumers whose rendering capabilities are not uniformly documented.
controls.limitation: An llms.txt or Markdown file may ease access, but neither guarantees citation nor rankings.
